title: IEA Chief: Electrification Still Energy's Top Bet Despite AI Fears
summary: Rising electrification rates remain the main pillar of global energy investment despite recent concerns about the existential threat that AI could pose for humanity, Fatih Birol, the Executive Director of the International Energy Agency (IEA), said on Thursday. “Electricity demand increases three times faster than the total energy demand,” Birol told a news conference in Seoul, as carried by Reuters. title: Ukraine Hits Refinery as Moscow Prepares to Extend Diesel Export Ban
summary: Ukraine hit overnight an oil refinery near Moscow, damaging a processing plant co-owned by Rosneft and Gazprom Neft, as Russia prepares to extend its ban on diesel exports through the end of October. In a sign that Ukraine and Russia have not agreed on any partial truce not to strike energy infrastructure, Ukraine's forces hit with drones the refinery in Yaroslavl, while Russia attacked infrastructure in Kyiv. The 300,000-barrels-per-day refinery in Yaroslavl, fewer than 200 miles northeast of Moscow, was hit overnight with drones in a joint operation…

title: Why the era of cheap government debt is over
summary: US debt has topped $40 trillion. How risky is the country's growing debt burden. And will investors keep funding Washington's deficits?

title: Federal Reserve: Higher-for-longer path reshapes cuts – Rabobank
summary: Rabobank's Senior Macro Strategist Bas van Geffen discusses the latest FOMC decision, noting a unanimous 25 bps hike in the Federal funds rate and a shift to a higher policy rate trajectory for similar inflation outcomes.

title: US Federal Reserve hikes interest rates for the first time in three years
summary: The US central bank raised its benchmark rate by .25 percent, with new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh defying President Donald Trump's desire for lower rates. Consumer banks and bond markets react. Also, OpenAI reveals new incidents of AI misconduct as fears grow that the technology could escape human control.

title: Horizontal or vertical?  Europeans invited to vote on future banknote designs
summary: People in the single-currency Eurozone have been invited to vote on the designs of upcoming euro bank bills. Proposed designs include historic figures like Marie Curie and Leonardo da Vinci, as well as a vertical format. They are expected to enter circulation around 2030. But first, as higher fuel prices stemming from the Iran war hurt consumers, fishermen in southern France scuffled with police as they tried to blockade an oil depot.
